analysis:
This batch changes documentation only. No provider source, wire protocol, crypto, attestation or cache code changed.

docs/operations/model-migration.md:
- Step 1 (head 79-84) now lets an operator reuse an existing valid canonical manifest and its serving files. In that case no R2 write credentials are needed, which narrows credential exposure. A backup URL with a different prefix or inventory still requires a new canonical publication.
- Head 142-145 rewords platform-owned HandleRegisterModel. Registration now validates manifest identity, declared inventory and file sizes. Base 137-138 said it also verified per-file hashes. The doc now says providers verify actual file hashes when downloading.
- Assessment: the manifest hashes remain the integrity anchor that providers enforce. Hash-mismatched or corrupted uploads now surface at provider download time, not at registration. That is an availability and operational issue, not a confidentiality or integrity regression for A-004, T-012 or T-027.
- The backend implementation is out of scope and was not supplied, so this rests on the doc's claim. A later pass should confirm the provider prefetch path (ProviderLoop+Prefetch.swift) still fails closed on a hash mismatch. It should also confirm that the catalog weightHash used for challenges and SSD cache binding (T-041) still comes from the manifest aggregate hash.

docs/developer/test.md:
- Adds a "Model publication workflow checks" section (head 444-456). It runs workflow tests against a loopback HTTP server with fixture credentials and states they never contact production.
- The rest is test guidance consistent with TB-011 and T-053 (resumption and logout tests) and T-041 (isolated cache keys, "never use production cache roots/keys" at line 163).
- No security claims are weakened.

docs/operations/model-revisions.md (47a2f33ed532c5e5:0): only metadata was supplied, with no content. Treat this as a coverage limit, not as evidence the change is safe.

No findings.
